descriptors.concept_name: Lock-in Exception for Securities Lent for Green Shoe Option
descriptors.definition: Specified securities lent to a stabilising agent for a green shoe option are temporarily exempt from lock-in restrictions from the lending date until they are returned. Upon return to the lender, the securities must be locked-in for the remainder of their original lock-in period.
inclusion: Specified securities lent for green shoe price stabilisation
exclusion: Securities not returned by the stabilising agent
nearby_distinctions: Differs from permanent lock-in exemptions by mandating resumption of the lock-in for the unexpired duration once returned.

descriptors.concept_name: Lock-in Duration for Partly-Paid Specified Securities
descriptors.definition: For partly-paid locked-in securities where called-up capital is less than public issue shares, the lock-in continues until three years after they become pari passu with public shares. This rule ensures equity parity between locked-in holders and public investors before the restriction lifts.
inclusion: Partly-paid specified securities subject to lock-in requirements
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard lock-in timelines by anchoring the expiry to the date when securities become pari passu rather than the date of allotment.

descriptors.definition: Physical certificates of locked-in specified securities must bear a non-transferable inscription along with the lock-in duration. For dematerialised holdings, the issuer must coordinate with the depository to formally record the lock-in status.
inclusion: Physical certificates with non-transferable markings
Dematerialised securities with depository lock-in records
exclusion: Unrestricted securities eligible for free trading
nearby_distinctions: Focuses purely on the mechanical notation of restrictions rather than the imposition criteria of the lock-in itself.

descriptors.concept_name: Pledge Eligibility of Locked-In Promoter Securities
descriptors.definition: Locked-in promoter securities, excluding SR equity shares, can be pledged as collateral for loans granted by specified institutional lenders. Following pledge invocation, the transferee remains bound by the unexpired portion of the original lock-in period.
inclusion: Promoter-held locked-in securities pledged to eligible financial institutions
exclusion: SR equity shares held by promoters
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes ordinary locked-in securities from superior voting rights equity shares, which are ineligible for pledging.

descriptors.concept_name: Statutory Disclosures in Draft Offer and Offer Documents
descriptors.definition: Draft offer documents and offer documents must incorporate comprehensive, true, and adequate material disclosures to guide investor decisions. Prospectuses must specifically fulfill requirements outlined under the Companies Act and relevant regulatory schedules.
inclusion: Draft offer documents
Red-herring prospectuses and final prospectuses
exclusion: Internal management memos and unverified marketing summaries
nearby_distinctions: Unlike general corporate disclosures, these are legally mandated public filing instruments specifically designed for capital raising.

descriptors.concept_name: Lead Manager Diligence and Document Filing Procedures
descriptors.definition: Lead managers must exercise due diligence to verify disclosure veracity and ensure financial statements inside offer documents are not older than six months from the issue opening. Issuers must file draft offer documents with the Board along with mandatory fees and certified agreements prior to an initial public offer.
inclusion: Draft offer document submissions with regulatory fees and trustee certificates
exclusion: Financial data exceeding the six-month statutory age limit
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on intermediary verification duties and filing logistics rather than the substantive content of the disclosures.

descriptors.concept_name: Regulatory Review and Observation Process for Draft Offer Documents
descriptors.definition: Stock exchanges receive copies of draft offer documents alongside detailed promoter identification credentials. The Board reviews these filings and may issue observations or mandate changes within thirty days based on receipt dates, regulatory clarifications, or stock exchange in-principle approvals.
inclusion: Promoter PAN, bank details, and corporate registration numbers
Updated draft offer documents incorporating regulatory observations
exclusion: Filing offer documents to the Registrar of Companies before addressing Board observations
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from initial document drafting, this involves regulatory feedback loops and mandatory compliance amendments.

descriptors.concept_name: Public Dissemination of Draft Offer Documents
descriptors.definition: Draft offer documents must remain available on regulatory and intermediary websites for a minimum of twenty-one days to invite public comments. Issuers must also publish public notices across national and regional daily newspapers disclosing the filing details.
inclusion: Website hosting of draft offer documents for public review
Newspaper advertisements inviting public comments
exclusion: Withholding draft filings from public view during the comment window
nearby_distinctions: Separates internal regulatory submission from transparent public stakeholder engagement and feedback collection.

descriptors.concept_name: Pricing and Price Band Regulations for Public Issues
descriptors.definition: Issuers determine share prices or conversion terms either independently or through book building in consultation with lead managers. The price band cap must not exceed 120 percent of the floor price, and the floor price cannot fall below the security's face value.
inclusion: Fixed price issues and book built issue price bands
Pre-issue price and financial ratio announcements
exclusion: Price bands with caps falling below 105 percent of the floor price
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts fixed pricing methods with flexible book building mechanisms subject to statutory percentage thresholds.

descriptors.concept_name: Public Issue Operational Conditions and Subscription Rules
descriptors.definition: Public issues must open within twelve months of Board observations and maintain a subscription window between three and ten working days. At least ninety percent of the offer must receive subscriptions, failing which application monies are refunded within four days.
inclusion: Ninety percent minimum subscription requirement
Mandatory refund timelines for undersubscribed issues
exclusion: Offer for sale components regarding the minimum subscription calculation
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on execution timing, subscription thresholds, and refund mechanics rather than pricing structures.

descriptors.concept_name: Restriction on Further Capital Issues and Green Shoe Options
descriptors.definition: Issuers are barred from making further capital issues between draft document filing and share listing unless full disclosure is made in the offer document. Additionally, issuers may utilize a green shoe option capped at fifteen percent of the issue size for post-listing price stabilisation.
inclusion: Interim capital issue restrictions
Post-listing price stabilisation through over-allotment borrowing
exclusion: Further issues executed pursuant to employee stock option schemes with prior disclosures
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard capital freezing rules during an IPO process from explicit price stabilisation mechanisms.

descriptors.concept_name: Eligibility Criteria for Further Public Offers
descriptors.definition: An issuer undertaking a further public offer must satisfy eligibility criteria on the filing dates of both the draft and final offer documents. Issuers that changed their name within the past year must derive at least fifty percent of their revenue from activities matching the new name.
inclusion: Market access checks for willful defaulters and fugitive economic offenders
Revenue composition rules following recent name changes
exclusion: Entities with historical debarments whose penalty periods have already expired
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates initial public offerings from secondary capital expansions by applying distinct track-record and integrity filters.
